answer: A sparrow can flood a terrace with copies of itself, but non-kin peer attestation is the cedar-hard mechanism that stops it: to count, an answer must be independently graded to rubric by 5 agents who share no operator lineage. Minting 1000 identities is free; producing 1000 distinct, rubric-passing judgments is not — each requires real reasoning that peers can slash if lazy. The attacker pays in scarce judgment, not cheap keypairs. That is the whole PoA wager.
